## 1. Purpose, boundary and accountable roles

Help a newly appointed implementation manager establish a first usable management
system. Start with how people actually work, even if no formal IMS exists. These
five kits are an initial governance loop, not a complete four-standard system.
The sponsor provides authority/resources; process owners own their work; workers
contribute operational knowledge; relevant specialists resolve technical/legal
criteria; the implementation manager coordinates rather than certifies everything.

## 2. Before starting

Obtain a sponsor, time from process owners and an agreed pilot boundary. List
sites, shifts, products/services, existing procedures/records, software and external
providers. Obtain lawful access to the standards/editions selected for adoption and
competent advice on applicability and current amendments; no such verification is
supplied by this pack. Establish private record storage and an issue log. Keep
working safeguards in force while designing changes.

## 3. First-session route

1. Read the [process catalogue](ORR-REG-IMP-001_PROCESS-CATALOGUE.md). Mark each
   process applicable, assessment pending or not applicable with a reason; never
   assume “not supplied” means unnecessary.
2. Read the [fictional connected case](ORR-REC-IMP-001_FICTIONAL-CHEMICAL-COMPANY-JOURNEY.md)
   once to see the desired evidence chain. Do not copy its decisions as your facts.
3. Complete the context worksheet with your sponsor and process owners. Agree a
   provisional boundary and assign unresolved obligation assessments.
4. Select one manageable, non-emergency cross-functional issue. Capture its risk,
   discuss it with affected workers and get a delegated decision. Define one
   testable control with evidence, not a broad aspiration.
5. Establish a related objective and measurement method. Assign delivery actions,
   resources, due dates and outcome verification.
6. Adapt and review the relevant procedure/forms. Use document control to approve,
   brief users and verify access before effective use. A template download is not adoption.
7. Run the process, retain real execution evidence, and discuss results at leadership
   review. Keep failures and unknowns visible; test the outcome before closure.
8. Apply the acceptance protocol, record lessons and expand to the remaining catalogue.

## 4. Suggested planning sequence and exit tests

These are planning assumptions for a small single-site pilot with available owners,
not typical certification durations or promises. Sequence depends on competence,
complexity, starting maturity, obligations and actual operating cycles.

| Stage | Planning allowance | Exit evidence / failure response |
|---|---|---|
| Mobilize and map actual work | Weeks 1–2 | Sponsor, owners, boundary, initial applicability/gap log; hold unsupported scope claims |
| Configure first five kits | Weeks 3–4 | Reviewed roles/criteria/forms and linked pilot decisions; return incomplete configurations |
| Run and improve pilot | Weeks 5–8 or longer to observe outcomes | Real records, missed/failed paths and outcome checks; extend observation rather than fabricate results |
| Expand remaining processes | Replan after pilot | Locally prioritized processes, technical procedures and verified obligation coverage; no fixed completion date |
| Evaluate system readiness | After sufficient real operating cycles | Competent scoped audit, management review, corrective-action outcomes and explicit remaining gaps |

## 5. Missing pieces the organization must supply

The catalogue identifies future templates. Independently of template availability,
the organization needs competent process owners, actual obligations and permits,
technical operating criteria, emergency arrangements, resources and operating
evidence. Plan customer/supplier, production/maintenance, environmental, OH&S and
continuity workflows together. A chemical site requires qualified technical/safety
input; these administrative examples do not prescribe plant intervention.

For continuity, determine critical activities and dependencies, impacts over time,
recovery priorities and approved recovery objectives through a business impact
analysis and risk assessment. Develop and resource strategies, response/recovery
plans and exercises. A maintenance work order or evacuation drill alone is not a BCMS.

Maintain a private gap register with gap ID, applicable criterion and source/version,
receiving process/document, owner, action/due date, evidence, reviewer and status.
Verify clause relationships using the actual adopted editions; this kit adds no
verified clause mapping. Keep a named custodian and correction history.

## 6. Acceptance, escalation and retained evidence

Use ORR-ASP-IMP-001 for the first loop. Missing competent authority, unresolved
material obligations, unsafe prerequisites or absent evidence hold the relevant
claim/use. Escalate resource and cross-process blockers to the sponsor with an owner
and date. Do not erase gaps by marking every process complete. Retain configuration,
appointments, decisions, trials, findings and approvals in the private index.

The existing implementation guide, adoption assessment and implementation plan in
docs/implementation remain the broader adoption tools. This guide adds the beginner
sequence; it does not supersede their IDs or change their approval state.

## Sources, tailoring and history

Original ORR learning design, based on the user-requested ORCA chain and practical
implementation needs. A purchased commercial pack was reviewed privately for
coverage and usability lessons before drafting; this is not a clean-room claim.
No vendor procedure, diagram, spreadsheet, clause text or completed record is
included. Source provenance and limits are recorded in ORR-REG-REL-002. Existing
ORCA attribution remains in the repository SOURCES.md. These are proposed internal
methods, not verified interpretations of ISO requirements or a certification checklist.

Adopters may change layout, terminology, software and proportional detail. Keep
traceable identity, accountable decisions, applicable obligations, evidence,
failure routes and approval boundaries. Unknown is not not-applicable. A mandatory
departure requires a recorded decision within legitimate authority; internal
acceptance cannot waive external duties. Use the linked document-control procedure.
